picks.rationale: Strongest, most concrete item: neural rendering (DLSS Multi Frame Generation up to 6X + path tracing with Ray Reconstruction) shipping in a marquee title today — a clear signal of how fast AI rendering is becoming default in real games.
picks.excerpt: id Software's DOOM: The Dark Ages expansion Revelations ships with neural rendering across the board — DLSS Multi Frame Generation up to 6X, Super Resolution, and path tracing with Ray Reconstruction (up to 310 fps at 4K on RTX 5090); Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced follows July 9.

picks.rationale: High actionability for working Unity devs — prompt-driven setup and debugging of animation state machines and behavior trees; distinct content from the already-published asset-audit (7/7) and scene-setup (7/8) demos.
picks.excerpt: Official Unity video shows Unity AI (Beta) setting up and debugging animation state machines, behavior trees, and transitions from prompts 'so you can focus on game feel' — a third pillar of the Unity AI workflow after the asset-audit and scene-setup demos.

picks.rationale: Novel, credible field report on the downstream cost of AI / vibe-coded projects — directly relevant to solo devs and small studios weighing AI codegen tradeoffs ('who fixes the fixes?').
picks.excerpt: A software team is charging up to $10,000 to 'fix' broken vibe-coded projects — using AI to clean up AI-generated code. A pointed snapshot of where the vibe-coding boom lands for small studios and solo devs: 'who fixes the fixes?'
